Revisiting the Collectathon: A Look at Indie 3D Platformers

Well, this article took nearly forever to write, since I had to research just about every major collectathon type platformer released by an indie team in the last three years.

But yeah, if you're waiting for Yooka-Laylee, some of the others on the list could be good games to play in the meantime.
Is this me or do all of these games use cartoony art style?

Yeah, they do. I suspect that's because they're pretty much all influenced by either Mario, Banjo-Kazooie, Conker, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro or Croc, which also all used cartoony art styles.

That and well... modern Mario and the Gamecube era seems to solidified the whole 'pastel colours with rounded edges on mostly square pieces of terrain' look that's almost become a symbol of the modern 3D platformer.
Would some deviations from this help to differentiate the game?

Yeah, it probably would. Probably would have helped the original games in the genre too, given how similar a lot of these games looked on the N64/PS1/Gamecube/PS2.

But for good or bad, a lot of people have seen the big titles in the area (think, A Hat in Time and Yooka-Laylee most of all) and decided that's what their indie platformer should look like too.
